_readme: Path rules for scripts/ci/risk-class.cjs in trustshell (owner policy r31, decision D-193). ADVISORY in CI: the workflow only prints a class. The merge gate outside this repo reads these rules from the BASE branch.

Per file the FIRST rule that matches, top to bottom, decides; the PR class is the HIGHEST class among its files. Order is load-bearing: self-protection first, then release and deploy authority, then the public verifier contract, then the tests carve-out, then guard/key/payment code, then the site, then docs.

Matchers: globs (** crosses directories, * does not, case-insensitive, anchored at the repo root); substrings (lowercased path contains it); tokens (a whole word of the path after splitting on non-alphanumerics and camelCase).
Anything no rule matches gets defaultClass (never LOW): unknown means one level up from what it looks like.
The script and workflow are copies of repid-engine's; only this rules file is specific to trustshell. All three are MAJOR to change (rule 1).
defaultReason: no rule matched: unknown paths go one level up from LOW, never LOW

packageJson.majorReason: package.json release fields changed (version/private/publishConfig/bin/files/exports/main/prepublishOnly): this is what npm publishes
packageJson.unknownReason: package.json changed and the release fields could not be compared: unsure goes up
packageJson.otherReason: package.json changed, release fields untouched (dependency or script change)

rules.reason: self-protection: the classifier's own rules, script or workflow; a PR must not lower its own class
release and CI authority: code owners, npm publish, release and extension packaging workflows
agent permission model: Claude settings and hooks, MCP server config
deploy and environment config, package registry config
license text: legal and irreversible once public
public verifier contract: receipt schemas and conformance vectors that outside verifiers build against
browser extension manifest: permissions granted in a user's browser
built output that ships in the npm package: reviewed with the release, never on its own
guard, sandbox and policy code: what stops an agent's action
answer-key is an eval answer key, not a credential: ordinary content
public-claim surface: narrowing a claim is LOW, a new claim is MAJOR, a path cannot tell, so one level up from docs
agent instructions and skills: they steer agents, so one level up from docs
CI config: workflows can read secrets and switch gates off, so one level up from tooling
path names money, keys/secrets, signing, custody, auth, grants, attestation, on-chain or settlement
tooling config that ships nothing: ignore files, lint and jest config
the public site: pages, components and static files strangers see
live behaviour: CLI, SDK, library, scripts, extension code, examples, lockfile and build config
